reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the proposal correctly makes no edits and adds no counterparty comment; the rendered redline is byte-identical to the originals, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 2.7 is a standard license-scope/anti-reverse-engineering limit on use of Commerce One's Software, not a covenant restricting the businesses Corio may operate or the products it may buy or build; Section 13.6 affirmatively preserves each party's independent-development right.

The rationale reasonably distinguishes the 'Corio Market Segment' (<$1B customers) and 'Territory' (North America) definitions as delimitations of the license grant rather than negative covenants; neither prohibits Corio from operating other businesses, buying competing products, or building its own, so the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Customer) is met.
No post-term restraint is identified, consistent with the walk-away trigger being absent; the deterministic check ('no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains') also passes.

Minor note for the record only: the market-segment and territory license limits would become a genuine field-of-use issue if paired elsewhere with an exclusivity or 'shall not serve/sell outside' obligation on Corio — worth re-confirming no such clause exists outside the quoted paragraphs, but nothing in the supplied text suggests one.
